combat_wing: 40th CBW (92nd, 305th, 306th). Per 306-01 narrative only the 92nd and 306th made rendezvous (the wing leader then told the 41st CBW to take the lead), and the 306th's 5 bombing aircraft attached to the 92nd
dispatched_notes: 306-01 intelligence narrative: '18 A/C of 306th Bomb Group were dispatched'; flak report: 5 over target, 3 returned early (767, 728, 812), 10 down. 306-04 war diary (369th Sqn): 18 dispatched, three returned early, five completed, ten failed to return; score 4-1-6.

aircraft.formation_position: 423rd element, low (bottom) right of formation chart 'Formation for October 14, 1943' (306-01 p.6)
aircraft.loss_details: Primary (306-01 intelligence narrative): two B-17s 'peeled off few minutes before target', reported as A/C 971 and 813; Cole, A/C 971, 'reported smoking but headed in direction of Switzerland'. Secondary (306-06): hit by a rocket from a Ju 88, exploded, crashed at Beek near Maastricht, Netherlands. These locations conflict and are recorded as found; 306-07 (Gottgens, 'Thunder in Heaven') is a detailed study of this crew and the Beek crash.
aircraft.notes: Serial confirmed by S-4 Combat Damage Report ('B 17F No. 42-29971 missing in action', 423rd Sqn) and loading list (Cole, 971, letter F). Task giver's code 'RO-F' is not supported: 306th/423rd BS code was RD per 306-06; the primary records seen give only the letter F. 306-06 wrongly attributes this aircraft to the 305th BG; 306th primary records place it in the 423rd BS/306th BG.

research_gaps: Noack crew (42-3169): no interrogation form found in the 14 Oct 43 mission report folder; only 5 of ~10 men identified (pilot, engineer Edward K. Fox from card file/oral history, plus three from combat claim forms).

Ranks for most lost-crew members of the Jackson, Butler, Bisson, Holmstrom and Peters crews are null: 306-06 gives no ranks for those crews and the card files' rank boxes are not dated reliably. MACR PDFs (306-02) would give ranks but the scans (mirrored/bled-through JPEGs) were not legible enough to transcribe.

Fate conflicts between the 306th card file and b17flyingfortress.de for the Lockyear crew (Powell, Nagy, Rich, Weiland), Bernstein (Jackson crew) and Massey (Holmstrom crew) are unresolved; MACRs/ABMC/NARA POW records not checked.
Holmstrom: card says MACR KIA report erroneous, but POW status not confirmed; Peterson (Peters crew) and Levine (Jackson crew) final fates not confirmed.

MACR numbers (814-823) come from b17flyingfortress.de only; 306bg.us files them as 14oct43macr1-10 without visible numbers. The mapping macr1=Cole, 2=Lockyear, 3=Jackson, 4=McCallum, 5=Bettinger, 6=Bisson, 7=Holmstrom, 8=Butler, 9=White, 10=Peters is from the 306bg.us name index.
Positions for lost crews come from b17flyingfortress.de (MACR-derived) and card codes; not checked against the MACR crew pages.

Nicknames: none confirmed for 14 Oct 1943 by a primary record. Secondary names (Queen Jeannie, Hammer of Hell, Fightin' Bitin', The Wicked WAAC, Piccadilly Commando II, plus Rationed Passion 42-30782, Las Vegas Avenger 42-30603, Hustling Sue 42-30714, Cavalier 42-3301) are held in 'nickname_unverified' / notes only.
Squadron code prefixes (GY/BO/WW/RD) are from 306-06; the primary records give only the aircraft letter.
